metadata.title: iGCSE History: Second World War Sample

questions.definition: A policy of giving in to some demands to avoid war.
questions.clue: Associated with Britain and France in the 1930s.
questions.explanation: Appeasement was used towards Hitler before the Second World War, partly because leaders wanted to avoid another major conflict.

questions.definition: A fast military tactic using aircraft, tanks, and infantry to overwhelm an enemy.
questions.explanation: Germany used blitzkrieg tactics in the early years of the war to defeat opponents quickly.

questions.definition: The alliance mainly made up of Germany, Italy, and Japan during the Second World War.
questions.explanation: The Axis Powers fought against the Allied Powers and aimed to expand their control in Europe, Africa, and Asia.

questions.definition: The countries that fought against the Axis Powers in the Second World War.
questions.clue: Included Britain, the Soviet Union, and the United States.
questions.explanation: The Allies cooperated militarily and economically to defeat Germany, Italy, and Japan.

questions.definition: The Allied landings in Normandy on 6 June 1944.
questions.clue: A major invasion of occupied France.
questions.explanation: D-Day opened a western front in Europe and was an important step towards the defeat of Nazi Germany.

questions.definition: The systematic murder of six million Jews and millions of other victims by Nazi Germany.
questions.clue: A genocide carried out during the war.
questions.explanation: The Holocaust was driven by Nazi racism and antisemitism and involved ghettos, mass shootings, concentration camps, and extermination camps.

questions.definition: The 1940 air battle in which Britain resisted German attempts to gain air superiority.
questions.clue: Fought mainly by the RAF and Luftwaffe.
questions.explanation: Britain's success prevented a German invasion and became a turning point in the early war.

questions.definition: The Japanese attack on a United States naval base on 7 December 1941.
questions.clue: Led the United States to enter the war.
questions.explanation: The attack brought the United States into the Second World War against Japan and then Germany and Italy.

questions.definition: A major battle where the Soviet Union defeated Germany in 1942-43.
questions.clue: A key turning point on the Eastern Front.
questions.explanation: The German defeat at Stalingrad weakened the Nazi war effort and marked a major shift in momentum.

questions.definition: The controlled distribution of scarce goods during wartime.
questions.clue: Used for food, fuel, and clothing.
questions.explanation: Rationing helped governments manage shortages and ensure fairer access to essential supplies.

questions.definition: The movement of people from dangerous areas to safer places.
questions.clue: Many children left cities during bombing.
questions.explanation: Evacuation in Britain aimed to protect civilians, especially children, from air raids.

questions.definition: An international organisation founded in 1945 to promote peace and cooperation.
questions.clue: Created after the Second World War.
questions.explanation: The United Nations was established after the war to reduce the chance of future global conflict.
